output.summary: The ED length-of-stay rise is almost entirely boarding (about 3.0 of 3.2 h), not ED work-up time. Boarding jumped in March-April, when the hospitalist rounding change moved medical-ward discharges later. Before-noon discharges fell from 29% to 9%. Surgical wards were unchanged. ED nurse staffing hours, vacancy and grid compliance are flat or better. Volume, acuity, beds and occupancy are flat. The 4 West huddle pilot looks causal: allocation came from a prior schedule, the groups were comparable, and the other wards showed no spillover. The evening bed-cleaning cut (September) is unquantified and boarding was already high before it. The loss of the triage provider on 1 May is a rival explanation for the door-to-provider and LWBS changes. Extend the huddle; do not commit to travel nurses.
